b: The University of Missouri (Mizzou) defeated the defending champions, University of Texas at Dallas (UTD) in an exciting final match of the Collegiate Chess League Fall 2026 (CCL). Mizzou couldn't hold onto their early lead, allowing the match to reach an 8-8 tie, leading to a winner-takes-all tiebreak match. In the tiebreaks, Mizzou swept all four games to take their first title since the Fall 2024 season.
Mizzou edged UTD in a tight final match.
In the first round, Mizzou took a decisive lead, winning three games and drawing one. GM Aryan Tari got off to a good start, winning with Black against GM Sankalp Gupta.
In the second round, UTD struck back, winning three games, drawing one, and evening the score. Gupta got back on track with a well-played win against GM Mahel Boyer.

After two back-and-forth rounds, the the match settled down in round three. Boyer won for Mizzou, while Gupta won again for UTD. GM Aditya Samant had a great chance to score another critical point, but allowed Tari to slip away, keeping the match tied.
For the second-straight round, neither side was able to break through in round four. Each team won two games, including this powerful performance by GM Rahul Srivatshav against Tari.

In the regular season, the match would have ended 8-8, but the CCL doesn't allow co-champions. The teams played one final round and Mizzou absolutely dominated. They won cleanly on every board to take the match 12-8. Boyer scored the final point to take the title.
You can watch the final match, hosted by Joe Lee.
The Collegiate Chess League is the premier online chess competition for college students.
NM Jeremy Kane is the Instructional Content Manager for Chess.com, and the author of several courses in the Starting Out series, Queen’s Gambit Accepted, Trompowsky, and Tarrasch.
